title: Sienna BioSystems inference cost reduction — exec sheet
summary: One-page workbook-style export that compares baseline inference spend vs. post-Redwood Optimize recommendations for Sienna BioSystems’ document-embedding and chat endpoints. Includes assumptions, model mix scenarios, sensitivity ranges, and recommended rollout actions targeted at reducing monthly spend while keeping P95 latency under 350ms.
assumptions: Baseline model mix: small-chat-v1 (generation) and sem-embed-3 (512-d). Token pricing: baseline $0.015 per 1k tokens (hosted), post-optimize effective token cost range assumes 2.0x throughput improvement and 3x prefix cache hit for repeated docs. Month = 30 days. Typical request profile: 65% embeddings, 35% chat/generation. SLO critical path: P95 latency <350ms on non-dedicated tier; target for Dedicated plan is <200ms.
key_numbers: Total baseline monthly spend: $71,213. Total post-optimize monthly spend (recommended mix): $25,507. Estimated monthly savings: $45,706 (~64%). Estimated annualized run rate savings: $548,472. Expected perf impact: 5–10% median latency improvement; P95 preserved by fallback to unquantized variant for 5% of requests.
before_after_comparison: High-level: embeddings yield the largest unit-cost savings due to quantization + batching; chat generation benefits from KV cache and batch packing but retains a small percentage of HD requests (5%) routed to standard variant for strict latency/quality. Baseline spend concentrated in generation tokens (52% of spend) while embeddings account for 48%. After Optimize: generation spend drops to 40% of spend, embeddings drop to 12% due to 3x effective reuse of cached vectors and smaller representation size.
recommendations: 1) Roll out quantized embedding model (quant-embed-3-8bit) to 80% of embedding traffic over 2 weeks with A/B evals on recall@10. 2) Enable prefix KV caching with a 30-day LRU window for frequently queried docs — expect 2.5–3x cache hits. 3) Configure request-level routing: latency-sensitive customers to standard-chat variant (5% traffic), cost-sensitive to quant-chat variant. 4) Autoscale burst capacity for generation to maintain P95 under 350ms during spikes (policy: 2x burst for 10 minutes). 5) Track per-route cost, recall degradation, and quality regressions tied to prompt eval set (weekly checks).
sensitivity_notes: Best case (cache hit 3.5x, quant speed-up 2.5x): monthly savings ~76%. Conservative case (cache hit 1.5x, quant speed-up 1.4x): monthly savings ~28%. Key risk: quality regression on embeddings for long-tail medical PDFs; mitigations include hybrid rerank and holdout QA test set with monthly monitoring.
next_steps: 1) Run 14-day A/B with 10% traffic to quant-embed and quant-chat variants (owners: Priya/Shah). 2) Add 'medical-docs' prompt set to eval harness and schedule nightly regression checks (owner: Rafael Mendes). 3) Prepare customer presentation and contract amendment for Dedicated plan option if performance tests show P95 <200ms (owner: Aisha Kumar). 4) Create Ops runbook for fallback rules and SLO alerts (owner: Evan Liu).
notes_to_self: Keep one unquantized replica in each region for canary routing. Validate embedding cosine drift after 1M queries. Watch for tokenization differences between sem-embed-3 and quant-embed-3-8bit during rollout.
audience: Sienna BioSystems product + infra leads, and customer success. Intended to support a pricing conversation for Dedicated capacity and a phased Optimize pilot.
